summary.headline: The Select Board awarded the Town Common fence repair bid, approved an architect contract for the Neary school project, and celebrated a $3.9M culvert grant.
summary.summary: The Southborough Select Board opened by recognizing six local high school recipients of town scholarships alongside State Representative Kate Donaghue. The board approved the contract with Tappe Architects for the Neary School Building feasibility study, appointed Mark Davis to the school building committee, and awarded a $70,500 base bid contract to Kneeland Construction to restore the Town Common fence. Members also celebrated receiving nearly $3.9 million in state culvert grants, processed annual committee appointments, and set plans for an upcoming FY27 goal-setting retreat.

topics.title: Town scholarship presentations
topics.summary: The board and Scholarship Committee Chair Lisa Braccio presented town scholarships and legislative citations to six local students. State Representative Kate Donaghue presented formal citations from the Massachusetts House of Representatives honoring each recipient.
key_details: Claire Tang received the Southborough Town Scholarship and will attend New York University.
Joseph Truman received the Southborough Town Scholarship and is studying civil engineering at UMass Lowell.
Stephen Hoadley received the Linda Hubley Memorial Scholarship and will attend Boston College for human-centered engineering.
Daniel McGauley received the Southborough Town Scholarship to study marketing and finance.
Madeleine Lapham received the Stefanie Reineris Memorial Scholarship to attend Smith College for psychology.
Elizabeth Caffrey received both the Stefanie Reineris and Carroll Harris Memorial scholarships to attend Endicott College for early childhood education.

topics.title: Board updates, Memorial Day, and S&P bond rating
topics.summary: The chair and members delivered administrative updates covering municipal finances, community events, and departmental activities. Standard and Poor's renewed Southborough's AAA rating on general obligation bonds, though the rating agency warned of shrinking levy capacity and low reserves compared to peer municipalities.
key_details: S&P renewed the town's AAA general obligation bond rating and top short-term note rating, but noted low reserve levels.
The hearing room audio-visual upgrades were completed using cable PEG capital funds from Verizon, Charter, and Comcast.
Members reported on the Memorial Day ceremonies held indoors at the senior center and the newly debuted fire department honor guard.
A board member presented photos from live high-heat structural burn training attended with the fire department.
The town held a productive coordination meeting regarding the Hopkinton water connection project, with hopes to execute an Intermunicipal Agreement over the summer.

topics.title: Continued public hearing on Parkerville Road utility pole
topics.summary: The board reviewed a petition by National Grid for a new utility pole on Parkerville Road. A board member, the DPW superintendent, and an abutting resident conducted a site walk and agreed on an alternate location over the culvert where no immediate abutters are affected.
key_details: National Grid proposed installing a new utility pole on Parkerville Road.
A site walk identified an alternate location across a culvert in the woods away from nearby homes.
National Grid had not yet formally responded to the newly agreed site.
topics.outcome: Public hearing continued to June 16, 2026 at 6:30 PM.

topics.title: State culvert grant and One Stop grant updates
topics.summary: The board announced Southborough received nearly $3.9 million from the Massachusetts Community Culvert Grant Program for culvert infrastructure replacements. Because Town Meeting previously approved $3.9 million in borrowing for the work, the grant funding will allow the town to avoid taking on new debt.
key_details: Southborough was awarded $3,891,000 out of $35 million in statewide construction grants (roughly 10 percent of all construction funds distributed).
Town Meeting previously authorized $3.9 million in borrowing that can now eventually be rescinded.

The town is submitting a follow-up One Stop grant application for wayfinding signage design and development, as well as a $1 million grant application for water infrastructure in Southville and Cordaville.
topics.outcome: Grant award reported; follow-up applications underway.
topics.why_it_matters: The $3.9 million grant relieves taxpayers from having to borrow funds to finance major culvert replacements.

topics.title: Elementary school building committee feasibility study contract
topics.summary: The board reviewed and approved the contract with Tappe Architects for the Neary Elementary School feasibility study. Members clarified that the designer must objectively study both options approved by Town Meeting without eliminating either before Town Meeting gets to decide.
key_details: The contract retains Tappe Architects for feasibility and schematic design work for the Neary school project.
Board members debated contract language adapted from standard MSBA boilerplates to ensure both Town Meeting options receive full cost analysis and drawings.
The architect will prepare equal cost evaluations and preliminary designs for both options ahead of Town Meeting.
topics.why_it_matters: The architectural feasibility study determines the options and costs presented to voters for modernizing or rebuilding the town's elementary school facilities.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The board approved consent agenda items and amended minutes from the May 19 meeting, then voted to enter executive session regarding real estate.
key_details: Approved consent agenda items B, C, E, and G.
Approved amended open session minutes of May 19, 2026.
Voted to enter executive session under Exemption 6 to discuss Chapter 61A real estate on Northborough Road.
topics.outcome: Routine motions and executive session entry approved.

topics.title: Annual board and committee reappointments
topics.summary: The Select Board considered the annual slate of reappointments for town boards and committees whose terms expire June 30. Members voted to reappoint all incumbents seeking reappointment, holding two specific seats for discussion at the upcoming goal-setting session, and later appointed two new members to the Cultural Arts Council.
key_details: Reappointments across town committees were approved 5-0.
Reappointments for Freddie Gillespie (Open Space and Stewardship) and Kelly O'Brien (Historical Commission) were held pending the board's retreat.
Karen Trachtenberg and Martha Bruehl were appointed to the Southborough Cultural Arts Council for three-year terms ending June 30, 2029.
topics.outcome: Slate of committee reappointments approved 5-0; two new Cultural Arts Council members appointed 5-0.

topics.title: Elementary school building committee appointment: Mark Davis
topics.summary: The board interviewed resident Mark Davis for an open position on the Elementary School Building Committee. Davis emphasized his real estate and construction background with the MBTA and stated his commitment to objectively gathering facts on both Town Meeting options.
key_details: Mark Davis previously served on the Neary Building Committee and finance subcommittees.
Davis noted that timing makes it unlikely to bring final school proposals to a fall 2026 Special Town Meeting.
Member Tim Fling voted against the appointment following previous disagreements on committee direction.
topics.outcome: Mark Davis appointed to the Elementary School Building Committee 4-1.

topics.title: Town Common fence and railing bid award
topics.summary: DPW Superintendent Bill Cundiff joined the board to present bids for the Town Common fence and railing restoration project, which was funded with $120,000 in Community Preservation Act funds. The board voted to award the base bid to Kneeland Construction to repair and restore the existing fence.
key_details: Kneeland Construction submitted the lowest eligible base bid at $70,500.
Additional engineering and construction oversight will bring the base project cost to roughly $82,000 to $83,000.
Procurement rules prevented skipping Alternate 1 (full replacement, over budget) to award Alternate 2 (replacing a section lost during a state highway project).
The town will separately pursue MassDOT to replace or fund the missing fence section, or issue a separate bid later.
topics.outcome: Base bid awarded to Kneeland Construction 4-1 (Fling opposed).
topics.why_it_matters: The vote commits CPA historic preservation funds to restore the deteriorated railing and fencing surrounding the Town Common.

topics.title: FY27 goal setting retreat planning and office hours
topics.summary: The board discussed logistical preparations and goal submissions for its upcoming FY27 goal-setting retreat. Members agreed to submit up to 10 prioritized goals each by Thursday morning for compilation into a master spreadsheet.
key_details: The goal-setting retreat is scheduled for Monday, June 8, 2026, at 6:00 PM at the Public Safety Building.
Each member will submit no more than 10 goals by Thursday morning to avoid overburdening the agenda.
Members discussed tracking multi-year carryover priorities including wastewater planning and commercial tax base expansion.
Select Board office hours are planned for Tuesday, June 9, 2026, at 6:00 PM.
topics.outcome: Goal submission deadline set for Thursday morning.

votes.motion: Continue the public hearing for the National Grid pole on Parkerville Road to June 16, 2026 at 6:30 PM
Approve the contract with Tappe Architects for the Neary school project feasibility study

Approve the amended open session minutes of May 19, 2026
Reappoint all committee members seeking reappointment as listed, holding Freddie Gillespie and Kelly O'Brien
Appoint Mark Davis to the Elementary School Building Committee for a term ending when the Select Board deems work complete
Award the base bid for the Town Common fence and railing project to Kneeland Construction
Appoint Karen Trachtenberg and Martha Bruehl to the Southborough Cultural Arts Council effective June 30, 2026 for three-year terms
